t: That that portion of Boston Inner Harbor and Fort Point Channel in Suffolk County, Commonwealth of Massachusetts, lying within the following described urea is hereby declared to be not a navigable water of the United States within the meaning of the laws of the United States: Beginning at the intersection of the northeasterly sideline of Northern Avenue and the westerly United States Pierhead Line of the Fort Point Channel and running northwesterly by the northeasterly sideline of Northern Avenue to the westerly sideline of Atlantic Avenue; thence turning and running northerly and northwesterly by the westerly sideline of Atlantic Avenue, and of Commercial Street to the southeasterly sideline of Hanover Street; thence turning and running northeasterly by the southeasterly sideline of Hanover Street to the southwesterly property line of the United States Coast Guard Base; thence turning and running southeasterly by the southwesterly property line of the United States Coast. Guard Base to the southeasterly property line of the United States Coast Guard Base; thence turning and running northeasterly by the southeasterly property line of the United States Coast Guard Base extended to the United States Pierhead Line; thence turning and running southeasterly, southerly and southwesterly by the United States Pierhead Line, to the point of beginning.

fable.w: This section is a direct congressional declaration that a described portion of Boston Inner Harbor and Fort Point Channel is not navigable water, followed by a metes-and-bounds description. The tempting reading is that naming the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, Suffolk County and local streets implies state or local involvement, but those are only geographic references. No consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue involving any non-federal party is provided.
fable.s: is hereby declared to be not a navigable water of the United States within the meaning of the laws of the United States

qwen_block.w: This section is a declaratory provision defining the legal status of a specific geographic area (declaring it not a navigable water of the United States). It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, advisory boards, or hearings. It is a unilateral legislative determination of fact/status, not a participatory mechanism.
qwen_block.s: That that portion of Boston Inner Harbor and Fort Point Channel in Suffolk County, Commonwealth of Massachusetts, lying within the following described urea is hereby declared to be not a navigable water of the United States within the meaning of the laws of the United States

opus.w: Congress itself declares part of Boston Inner Harbor and Fort Point Channel non-navigable. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with states or others, or right to sue is provided. The mentions of the Coast Guard Base and the Pierhead Line only mark the boundary and involve no outside party in any federal decision.
opus.s: is hereby declared to be not a navigable water of the United States within the meaning of the laws of the United States
opus.b: **Tempting reading:** Federal entities and federal law come up ("the laws of the United States," "United States Coast Guard Base"), so it might seem that some federal decision process is involved. That reading fails. Congress is making the decision directly here, and the federal references only describe the area's boundaries. No outside party is consulted, given a hearing, or given a right to sue.
